v.rationale: impl-1 is the most complete and idiomatic: the ownership check sits on the route, the queue settings use current attributes, the job is re-runnable, it handles the byte-order mark, and missing files and bad headers both record a clear reason. Its tests are the best of the three, and the only issue found is cosmetic (null counts in the 202 response). impl-2 has many good choices (Sanctum, WithoutRelations, model defaults, batched errors, strong tests) but a real correctness bug: CSVs that start with a byte-order mark, common from Excel, fail entirely. It also relies on the default fgetcsv escape and adds Dispatchable twice. impl-3 is lean and uses modern touches (File rule, afterCommit, WithoutTimestamps), but a missing file crashes with a TypeError, the failure reason is thrown away, there are no retries, the factory has no user, two tables share one migration, and the test suite is thinner. impl-2 edges out impl-3 because its bug is narrower and its tests are clearly stronger.
